architecture.mechanism: Closed-loop compensation of XY gantry positioning error by correlating barcode-reader-derived vial identity with a peristaltic-probe contact-based fiducial measurement, using the locking carousel lid as a rigid reference plane to suppress thermal and mechanical drift between successive index moves.
architecture.intervention: Add a low-cost capacitive or force-sensing contact probe to the peristaltic sample probe tip; after each gantry move to a target vial, perform a short vertical descent until the probe touches the vial septum, record the actual XY position at contact, and use the deviation from the commanded position to update a per-vial error map stored in firmware; the locking carousel lid is instrumented with three fixed reference pins that the probe touches periodically to re-zero the map, and the vial-present sensor is used to gate the correction only when a vial is actually present.
architecture.expected_effect: Reduction of mean absolute XY positioning error from the current unspecified baseline (assumed >0.5 mm) to below 0.1 mm for 95% of index moves, with a corresponding decrease in probe misalignment and sample carryover, measured over 1000 consecutive vial-to-vial moves.
architecture.falsification_test: Run 200 consecutive moves to a single vial without re-zeroing; if the error map does not converge to a stable correction (i.e., residual error remains >0.2 mm after 50 moves), the mechanism fails. Cheapest test: use a calibrated microscope stage to measure actual probe tip position after each move, without any contact sensing, and compare to commanded positions.
